summary: Service account impersonation scoping prevents delegated admin operations in private prod
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that new service account tokens cannot perform delegated admin ops (user management and billing read) after migrating to a private deployment token broker. Impact: Multiple automation jobs and SRE runbooks fail; customer-facing admin UI returns 403 when acting-as a service account. Environment: Private deployment (Aurora private VPC), prod - us-east, Redwood private control plane with identity-proxy v1.9.2 and token-broker v0.8.2. Observed start: 2026-03-09 18:20 UTC. Business impact: Blocks Aurora's automated onboarding and scheduled invoice exports; they are a HIPAA-regulated customer and cannot proceed with several tasks until impersonation works.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create service account 'onboard-runner@aurora' in Aurora tenant. 2) Request token via Aurora's token-broker that exchanges internal long-lived key for a short-lived access token. 3) Call Admin API /v1/admin/users with X-Redwood-Impersonate header set to 'user:alice@aurora.com' and Authorization: Bearer <token>. 4) Observe 403 'insufficient_scope' returned. 5) Same call with the original human user's token succeeds.
logs_snippets: identity-proxy (2026-03-09T18:21:12Z) WARN request_id=3fa2ed 'token scope mismatch: expected [admin:impersonate,admin:users] got [service:read,service:write]'; admin-api (2026-03-09T18:21:12Z) ERROR request_id=3fa2ed 'authorization failed for impersonation: missing permission admin:impersonate'; token-broker (2026-03-09T18:20:58Z) INFO 'issued token sub=svc:onboard-runner aud=redwood-api scope="service:read service:write" exp=2026-03-09T19:20:58Z'
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: token-broker is attaching default service scopes rather than tenant-mapped impersonation scopes. Confirmed that tenant mapping rule set 'aurora-mappings' in token-broker was not applied after the private control-plane upgrade (v0.8.0->v0.8.2). Identity-proxy performs additional scope filtering: it strips any scope not in allowed_scope_table for service accounts. Allowed_scope_table for Aurora appears to be stale and only lists 'service:*' scopes. Replayed token exchange locally with debug flags: mapping step returned intended impersonation grant, but the token-broker's caching layer served an earlier cached token profile. Cache invalidation appears tied to last-deploy timestamp; deployment delta on 2026-03-08 likely left cache entries inconsistent. Cross-referenced with INT-4112 where SRE rolled out token-broker config but noted a missing cache-buster flag. Observed related PR that changed default scopes (see related_github_prs).
workaround: Temporary workaround provided to customer: 1) Use a human admin token for critical admin calls. 2) As short-term automated fix, update identity-proxy config to whitelist the service account 'onboard-runner@aurora' with an explicit mapping to include admin:impersonate and admin:users. Provided steps and a patch snippet to Aurora engineering. Note this bypass is allowed only in their private VPC and will be removed after full fix.
resolution: Investigating full fix: coordinated deploy sequence to invalidate token-broker cache and roll token-broker + identity-proxy together with a cache-buster flag. SRE to schedule an out-of-band config reload for Aurora's token-broker and then redeploy identity-proxy v1.9.3 which contains a protective check to reject stale cached scope profiles. After reload, verified token exchange returns token with scopes [admin:impersonate,admin:users] and admin API calls succeed. Resolution steps documented in confluence page and will be included in a postmortem. Customer notified and temporary whitelist removed. Planned follow-up: add integration test in CI to simulate config drift and prevent mapping cache staleness.
